title: Form
description: One listed form: a spelling with an apostrophe or hyphen whose letters are one word of the vocabulary. One line of data/vocabulary/forms.jsonl. Apostrophes, hyphens and punctuation carry no letters, so the search knows only the letters-word; the form is how that word is shown when it is the only spelling of its letters, and is listed beside the word otherwise. Every form is public, carries a meaning a reader can read, and names where it is attested; the operator accepts it by merging the pull request that adds it. Possessives are never listed.

form.description: The spelling as it reads: lowercase letters with at least one apostrophe or hyphen, nothing else. Capitals belong to a hit's display, never to a form.

letters.description: The word the form's letters spell, as the search knows it: the form with its apostrophes and hyphens dropped. The tools derive and check it.

kind.description: contraction: an apostrophe stands for letters left out (it's, don't). hyphenated: a term written with hyphens (jack-o'-lantern).

gloss.description: What the form means, in one sentence. A reader sees this in the word panel, so PRODUCT.md's rule applies: a capital letter at the start and a full stop at the end.

trace.description: Where the form is attested: a public URL, usually its Wiktionary entry.

proposed_by.description: Who proposed it. The routine and the Build page propose; only a merge admits.

pos.description: The parts of speech the form can be, for the order words read in. Used only when the letters-word is not in English OpenList, which has no tags for it; a word the pinned list has keeps the dictionary's own.

note.description: Anything else worth recording about the admission.
